user.title: Choose how to sign in
user.description:
**Samsung Account (recommended)**: sign in once on Samsung's own page; Home Assistant renews the session by itself afterwards.

**Cookie**: copy the `JSESSIONID` from a logged-in browser. Quick to set up, but it has to be replaced when it expires (measured: gone after ~18 h idle).

account.title: Samsung Account sign-in
account.description:
**Step 1**: open the developer tools (`F12`) in a new tab -> **Network** -> tick **Preserve log**.

**Step 2**: select the whole sign-in link in field **①** (`Ctrl+A`, `Ctrl+C`), paste it into that new tab and sign in on Samsung's page (password and second factor are only typed there).

> The link is ~1800 characters long; do not copy it from the page text, that only gives the Home Assistant address.

**Step 3**: when the sign-in ends the browser tries to open `ms-app://...` and fails - that is expected. Type `ms-app` in the Network filter, right-click the request -> **Copy -> Copy URL** (the red message in the Console contains the address too).

**Step 4**: paste that whole `ms-app://...` address into field **②** and submit.

The link is valid for 15 minutes. Only the `userauth_token` is stored, never the password.

data.signin_url: ① Sign-in link (click, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C, open in a new tab)
data.callback_url: ② Paste the ms-app:// callback here
data.device_name: ③ Device name (shown in the Samsung Account device list)

cookie.title: Paste a cookie
cookie.description:
1. Log in at https://findmymobile.samsung.cn in a desktop browser.
2. Press `F12` -> **Application** -> **Storage -> Cookies** -> `https://findmymobile.samsung.cn`.
3. Copy the value of **`JSESSIONID`** (it is `HttpOnly`, so the Console cannot see it).
4. Paste it below. A full `Cookie: ...` header works as well.

The Samsung password is never needed here.

data.jsessionid: JSESSIONID value (or a full Cookie header)

init.title: Samsung Find options
init.description:
**Passive**: only read the last position Samsung already has - no extra battery use; how fresh it is depends on the device's own reporting.

**Active**: additionally ask the device to locate itself now (at most once per "minimum auto-refresh interval"). Fresher positions, but it wakes the device and uses more battery.

Both modes can be set separately for phones/tablets/watches/earbuds and for SmartTags.

> To refresh once on demand use the device's *Refresh location* button instead of enabling active mode.
> With cookie authentication you can also paste a new cookie here to replace the session.

data.cookie: New cookie (leave empty to keep the current session)
data.mode_others: Mode for phones / tablets / watches / earbuds

data_description.cookie: Only needed when the current cookie expired; it is validated before it is stored.
data_description.mode_others: Passive = read only; active = ask the device to locate once per update.
data_description.mode_smarttags: Tags are located through nearby Galaxy devices, so active mode costs little.
data_description.update_interval: How often Home Assistant reads from Samsung. Minimum 30 s.
data_description.active_interval: Minimum time between two automatic location requests to the same device. Requests are only sent on updates, so the real interval is rounded up to the next update.
data_description.max_location_age: After this the tracker stops reporting the old position (state unknown), so `person` falls back to its other trackers; 0 keeps showing the last position.

options.passive: Passive: read Samsung's last position (almost no battery use)
options.active: Active: make the device locate itself (fresher, more battery)

location_not_allowed.title: Samsung Find: a device is not allowed to report its position
location_not_allowed.description:
The device(s) {devices} have not accepted Samsung's location / personal data terms, so positions never update (requests are accepted but the device never answers).

Open https://findmymobile.samsung.cn, accept the dialog and reload the integration.

This notice disappears by itself once the consent is given.
